newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down despite high rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down despite high rates.

text.p: * Banks building up long dollar positions
The Philippine peso ended weaker on Monday at a day-low of 26.269 pesos from 26.268 despite the high interest rates in the money market, traders said.
The high overnight rates should have sent banks selling their dollars to generate peso liquidity.
Instead, "a lot of banks are going long on dollars," a foreign bank dealer said, adding that they see the high overnight rates as temporary.

Following Friday's news of a 4.4 percent inflation in September, "there is pressure for the Central Bank to lower its overnight rates. The advantage of the peso over the dollar will be cut drastically," the same dealer said.
This widely-held view was firmed up when Treasury bill rates dropped across all maturities on Monday even though overnight rates jumped to a high of 13.5 percent.
The day's average was at 26.266 pesos versus 26.264 on Friday, with turnover thinning to $84.0 million from $123.25 million.
